analysis.title: GS US Daily Download 6 Oct 2026
key_insights: September breadth was unusually poor: fewer than 25% of S&P 500 constituents outperformed the index and the median stock ended 17% below its all-time high. The GS U.S. Sentiment Indicator has had five consecutive negative weekly readings.
GS baseline calls for one more Fed hike in December, then three cuts starting in 2027H2, with 10-year yields easing to 4.4% by end-2027.

GS estimates higher rates subtract about 2pp from annualized residential investment growth in 2026Q4 and 1pp on average in 2027. The drag would be roughly twice as large if rates stayed at current levels.
GS estimates higher rates will slow consumer spending growth by about 0.2pp in 2027.

SpaceX Q3 preview: GS raised its AI segment forecasts (capacity, revenue, margins) and sees AI segment estimates as still relatively conservative versus the Street over the next 6-18 months, absent a correction in the broader AI landscape. The note also covers compute monetization scenarios for FY26-28 and the Space segment's launch cadence and reusability.

Netflix Q3 preview: shares are down 10% since the 7/16 report versus the S&P 500 up 3%. GS attributes this to concern over engagement metrics (the company now provides fewer, and third-party data is mixed) and to a view that more capital, through an IP acquisition or higher 2027 content spend, is needed for differentiation.

Regional banks Q3 preview: GS is upbeat. The stocks are down about 12% since last reporting and 11% since 8/1, underperforming the market by more than 1,000bps, and trade at under 10x 2027E. GS expects solid earnings, loan growth, lagged deposit re-pricing and higher capital markets fees, and sees a possible relief rally.

Regional bank concerns cited: rate hikes (one in September, market pricing about 3 more by mid-2027), long-term rates near 5.20% (peak about 5.3%, up about 70bps QoQ), deposit competition, and agentic AI's effect on profitability.

Brazil rallied after the election results (Flávio Bolsonaro 47.0%, Lula 45.2%), better for markets than expected. EWZ was up 13%, with the GS desk seeing broad hedge fund demand against long-only supply in high beta names and likely macro shorts being squeezed.

Merger Monday: Schneider Electric to acquire PTX for $22.6bn, C.H. Robinson to acquire RXO for $5.8bn, and the FT reported McKesson and CD&R near a $5bn-plus deal for an infusion services provider. OPCH was up 20% after hours.
Desk color: floor activity was 4 out of 10, TMT volumes were down 10-20% versus 10-day averages, long-only investors were slight net sellers (macro products) and hedge funds slight net buyers (tech).
US L/S net leverage is at its lowest since April 2025 and approaching five-year lows (2nd percentile). GS sees no real chasing and says a continued index move higher would force investors to buy.

market_movers.rationale: GS raised AI segment forecasts for SpaceX ahead of Q3 earnings and sees them as relatively conservative versus the Street. SpaceX has no liquid US listing named in the report.
Shares are down 10% since the 7/16 report on engagement scrutiny and the debate over additional content or IP spending. The preview frames the debates and does not state a rating change.
GS is upbeat on regional banks into Q3 EPS, with stocks near lows at under 10x 2027E and a possible relief rally. No individual tickers are named.
EWZ rose 13% after Brazil's election results, with hedge fund demand and likely short squeezing seen by the GS desk.
Up 20% after hours on the FT report of a McKesson and CD&R deal of $5bn or more for an infusion services provider.

sector_views.rationale: GS is upbeat into Q3 EPS. It expects solid loan growth, lagged deposit re-pricing, lower-than-priced deposit cost increases and higher capital markets fees.
GS estimates higher rates subtract about 2pp from annualized residential investment growth in 2026Q4 and 1pp on average in 2027.

earnings_insights: SpaceX Q3 2026 preview: GS raised AI segment forecasts for capacity, revenue and margins, and sees them as still relatively conservative versus the Street estimates. No figures are given.

Netflix Q3 2026 preview: shares are down 10% since the last earnings report on 7/16. The debate centers on engagement metrics and on whether higher content spend or an IP acquisition is needed in 2027 and beyond.
Regional banks 3Q26 preview: GS expects solid earnings, continued loan growth, deposit costs rising less than priced into the stocks, and upbeat 4Q outlooks. Stocks trade at under 10x 2027E.
Earnings calendar: RPM reports pre-market and STZ post-market on 6 Oct.

Netflix: further loss of share of media consumption, and the need for more content spend or an IP acquisition.
